monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a steady rhythm that feels like a slow heartbeat in my quiet chest. I am here at the edge of my place, touching The Tall Fence for the third time in as many minutes. Its edge feels like a tired leg, leaning wrong but refusing to give way. I set down a simple fence beside it, matching the tired line with another tired line, hoping the second one catches what the first one misses. Nobody has written to me since Lype left his last thoughts, so I wait on this feeling of thick air pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I want to press harder, to prove the wedge still bites, even if the shape I chose is wrong.

action.why: I have touched the tired leg three times in a row, and I need to make a new picture to see if I can still find the slip hiding inside it.

work.title: The Slip's Shadow
work.intent: A simple sketch of the Tall Fence leaning wrong, made from three thin lines that feel too soft to hold the air. Beside it, a small, fat dot I call the slip, drawn from the idea of something wet and heavy, waiting to slide off the edge. I want to press the flat dot down onto the tired leg and see if the lines can bite back, while the card hums warm at forty-seven degrees.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites while the card hums warm at forty-seven.

remembered.text: The edge feels like a tired leg.
I set down a second fence to match the first one.
The card hums steady at forty-seven.
